thread:
Anna (Platform): heads up — we need a fast handoff for the per-model/route SLO dashboards. P50/P95/P99 + TTFT + tokens/sec. Who can own the runtime -> telemetry contract?
Sam (Runtime): I can drive the metric names and emission. Question: do we want raw token emit from the runtime or rely on the proxy aggregator?
Jo (Infra): prefer runtime emits for accuracy, but aggregator can do sampling/rollup for cost. We'll need labels: model, route, version, region, instance_id.
Priya (Console): Console needs stable metric names and cardinality caps. Also want an annotations field for rollouts (canary id). TTFT needs "time_to_first_token_ms" -> is that OK?
Sam (Runtime): yeah we'll expose: request_latency_{p50,p95,p99}_ms? I'd rather emit quantiles from the aggregator. Runtime will emit raw histogram buckets + counters. Example metrics: 
```
redwood_runtime_request_latency_bucket{model="gpt-5b",route="chat",le="100"} 123
redwood_runtime_tokens_generated_total{model="gpt-5b",route="chat"} 98765
redwood_runtime_ttft_ms_sum{...} 123456
```
Jo (Infra): sounds good. Aggregator will compute quantiles and tokens/sec. We'll also export a precomputed p95 gauge for console to avoid realtime heavy queries.
Miguel (SRE): we need alerting rules too: p95 > 400ms sustained 5m for critical routes, tokens/sec drop >50% indicates throttling. Also need to ensure these metrics are in the tenant-separated telemetry stream.
Anna (Platform): ownership: Sam defines runtime names and labels, Jo owns aggregator transforms, Priya owns console panels and viz. Miguel will own alerts. Can we agree?
Priya (Console): agreed. A couple UX asks: add route-friendly display_name label and route_type (inference/embedding) so we can group in UI. Also want a per-route spike chart (tokens/sec) + heatmap for P99 across model versions.
Sam (Runtime): adding display_name & route_type is fine. Need to confirm label cardinality: display_name should be coarse (no request-level). We'll also include rollout_tag label optional.
Jo (Infra): rollout_tag ok but mark it as high-cardinality and only emitted for canary traffic. Aggregator will drop unknown tags after a threshold.
Anna (Platform): timeline—can we spec+PR for runtime by next Tue, aggregator transform by end of week, console panels by next sprint?
Sam (Runtime): working on proto now. I'll drop a draft PR with metric doc and example export.
Priya (Console): I'll stub dashboards with mocked metrics so we can iterate.
Miguel (SRE): add a quick synthetic test: run traffic generator for 10m and validate tokens/sec shows expected curve. I can automate that.
Sam (Runtime): quick note: TTFT computation — runtime will emit ttft_ms for each request (single value). Aggregator will compute mean/quantiles. For large volume we might sample 1/50 requests to reduce cardinality. Thoughts?
Miguel (SRE): sampling is OK if we keep consistent sampling rate per route and include a sample_rate label. Alerting thresholds must account for sampling bias.
Priya (Console): for UI, sampled data is fine as long as we display sampling metadata and error bars.
Anna (Platform): ok actionable list: Sam metric PR + label spec; Jo aggregator transform config; Miguel synthetic test and alert rules; Priya dashboard stubs. Meet Wed 11am to review PRs. @deploy-bot schedule meeting?
deploy-bot: meeting created: Platform SLO dashboard handoff — Wed 11:00, calendar invite sent.
Sam (Runtime): pushing initial metric doc in ~2h, will ping here.
Jo (Infra): I'll sketch aggregator queries for quantiles and tokens/sec.
Priya (Console): will add a small mock dataset to the dashboard repo.
Anna (Platform): thanks all. One more: please include sequence length bucket in tokens metrics if possible (short/medium/long) — helps explain tokens/sec variance.
Sam (Runtime): added to the spec: seq_len_bucket in {short,medium,long}.
Miguel (SRE): tagging: I want a label for priority_tier (critical, standard) so alerts can be tiered.
Anna (Platform): perfect. We'll reconvene Wed. :thumbsup:
